scenarioStory.history: Sudden onset of substernal chest pressure (8/10) radiating to the jaw while mowing the lawn approximately 25 minutes ago, associated with nausea, diaphoresis, and lightheadedness. Pain has not improved with rest. Denies prior episodes like this.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: 64-year-old male found seated, pale and diaphoretic, reporting 8/10 substernal chest pressure radiating to the jaw with associated nausea and dizziness. Radial pulses are weak. Initial vitals reveal marginal hypotension and relative bradycardia, both classic for right ventricular involvement in an inferior STEMI. → 12-Lead and V4R Acquired: The 12-lead confirms an inferior STEMI (ST elevation II, III, aVF) and the right-sided V4R lead confirms RV involvement. The crew must recognize that this patient's hypotension is preload-dependent and that fluid resuscitation must precede any nitrate administration. → Fluid Bolus Given: Following the 500 mL fluid bolus, the patient's blood pressure and heart rate improve modestly. Chest pain persists at 6/10. Given the still-marginal blood pressure, the crew weighs opiate analgesia over nitroglycerin per protocol and continues STEMI transport. → Transport En Route: The patient remains hemodynamically stable en route to the STEMI-capable facility. Pain is improved with morphine, blood pressure and heart rate remain adequate, and the receiving hospital has been notified for cath lab activation.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: 64-year-old male found seated, pale and diaphoretic, reporting 8/10 substernal chest pressure radiating to the jaw with associated nausea and dizziness. Radial pulses are weak. Initial vitals reveal marginal hypotension and relative bradycardia, both classic for right ventricular involvement in an inferior STEMI.
relatedChecklist: Apply oxygen only if hypoxemic, titrate to SpO2 94-98%
Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact

scenarioEvents.name: 12-Lead and V4R Acquired
scenarioEvents.description: The 12-lead confirms an inferior STEMI (ST elevation II, III, aVF) and the right-sided V4R lead confirms RV involvement. The crew must recognize that this patient's hypotension is preload-dependent and that fluid resuscitation must precede any nitrate administration.
relatedChecklist: Recognize inferior STEMI with RV involvement; withhold nitroglycerin until fluids given
Administer 500 mL NS IV bolus, pressure-infused over <15 min (up to 30 mL/kg goal = 2,700 mL for 90 kg patient)
Provide advance STEMI notification to receiving hospital

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid Bolus Given
scenarioEvents.description: Following the 500 mL fluid bolus, the patient's blood pressure and heart rate improve modestly. Chest pain persists at 6/10. Given the still-marginal blood pressure, the crew weighs opiate analgesia over nitroglycerin per protocol and continues STEMI transport.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and repeat 12-lead after fluid bolus
Morphine 9 mg IV (90 kg x 0.1 mg/kg; max initial dose 10 mg), used cautiously given borderline BP
Continue transport to STEMI-capable facility with early notification of changes

scenarioEvents.name: Transport En Route
scenarioEvents.description: The patient remains hemodynamically stable en route to the STEMI-capable facility. Pain is improved with morphine, blood pressure and heart rate remain adequate, and the receiving hospital has been notified for cath lab activation.
relatedChecklist: Continue serial vital sign reassessment en route, transmit final 12-lead to receiving facility

scenarioEvents.name: Nitro Given Without Fluids
scenarioEvents.description: Sublingual nitroglycerin was administered for chest pain before the RV-infarct hypotension was corrected with fluids. Venous return drops sharply, causing a precipitous fall in blood pressure and a compensatory rise in heart rate.
relatedChecklist: Recognize nitrate-induced hypotension from RV infarct; place patient supine
Rapid 500 mL NS IV fluid bolus, pressure-infused, repeat as needed toward 30 mL/kg (2,700 mL) goal
Consider norepinephrine 0.05-0.5 mcg/kg/min IV if hypotension is fluid-refractory
